questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location as my family is from Sweden as well as the history of Uppsala University

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy and the mobility office was very helpful

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Initial orientations and tips and tricks from fellow exchange students in my accomodation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy through the MyHousing offers that were available and sent to us before the exchange.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you live in Flogsta it is quite far and you'll definitely need a bike. Also be prepared for cultural differences when it comes to cleanliness and that the buildings are in quite rough condition. But at the same time I would say that this is the best offer available due to the social life.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The block-system was quite foreign to me and getting my courses to line up was a little bit stressful and a challenge.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The mobility office was very helpful in this regard tho and writing them to get suggestions on courses worked very well as well as them being open to changes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite succesful. I got what I wanted and even got to change a course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write the mobility office with questions and be sure to take your time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I felt that generally the level of the courses was very low as people came with a lot of different backgrounds which made the teaching pretty entry level. This was a little bit frustrating except for the course I took on the ethnology department in swedish.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I felt again that the teaching style was not as in depth as I was used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Culture and War
The craft of public speaking
Forestillingsverdener
War and Peace on Film

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Culture and War as the structure of reading a whole book a week was very interesting and gave me a lot. Also Sverker is very knowledgable and passionate in his field.
Forestillingsverdener as Birgitta is a very good teacher as well and you really get a lot of information in the relatively short duration of the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There could have been more different offers

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A gym with different sports offers, climbing gym. There was some different things, but a lot of them you kind of forgot about. And the nations of course.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Gasques, nations, sports

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travelling around the nordics. There's not a lot to do in Uppsala.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy as I'm danish, but swedish people are kind of closed off.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The swedish people being kind of closed off

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The 'cleanliness' and structure.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go in with an open heart and be ready to really emerge yourself in the experience (don't do it halfway). Do your homework/emerge yourself in the studies and social life around that - especially if you go by yourself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really. Become a part of the nations and get a bike. Be prepared for the darkness of nov-dec.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I feel like I became more of an adult and the student-teacher relationships are quite unique in Uppsala in the way that you can actually become 'friends' with your teachers so take advantage of that.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The darkness and social life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
